config.title: Build confirmation dialog service

intro.title: Build confirmation dialog service
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a reusable confirmation dialog service in JavaScript. You will create a function that displays a modal dialog to ask users for confirmation before proceeding with an action, such as deleting an item. The core concept is using JavaScript functions and DOM manipulation to dynamically show and hide dialog elements on a webpage. You will work with HTML elements, event listeners, and callback functions to handle user responses. This service helps improve user experience by preventing accidental actions in web applications.
intro.usecase: Confirmation dialogs are essential in production applications to prevent accidental data loss or irreversible actions. You'll see them in e-commerce platforms when removing items from a cart, in admin dashboards before deleting user accounts, and in content management systems when publishing or discarding draft changes. As a developer, implementing a reusable confirmation service ensures consistent user experience across your application while reducing code duplication. This pattern is particularly valuable in complex interfaces where users frequently perform destructive operations like bulk deletions, payment confirmations, or system configuration changes.

objectives: Construct a reusable confirmation dialog component with customizable messages
Implement a service function that triggers the dialog and returns a promise
Configure the dialog to accept user confirmation or cancellation
Integrate the dialog service into existing UI components
Initialize and control the dialog's visibility state programmatically
Bind user actions to resolve or reject the dialog promise
Manipulate the DOM to render the dialog dynamically when triggered

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and the useState hook.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing modules
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have React and useState available for building the confirmation dialog service.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're importing both React and useState from 'react'. Check your import statement syntax.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. You need to import both React and useState from 'react' using the import statement.

steps.title: Create ConfirmationDialog component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named ConfirmationDialog that returns null initially.
steps.hint: Define a component using either function declaration or arrow function syntax, and have it return null.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create ConfirmationDialog component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A ConfirmationDialog component is defined and returns null.
successCriteria: The component is named ConfirmationDialog and returns null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the component is named exactly ConfirmationDialog and returns null.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component wasn't created correctly. Check the name and that it returns null.

steps.title: Add props parameter to component
steps.instruction: Add a props parameter to the ConfirmationDialog component function that includes message, onConfirm, and onCancel properties.
steps.hint: The props parameter should be an object with three properties. You can destructure them directly in the parameter or access them as props.message, etc.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ConfirmationDialog component should accept a props parameter with message, onConfirm, and onCancel properties.
successCriteria: The component function has a parameter that includes message, onConfirm, and onCancel.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a parameter, but it might not include all three required properties (message, onConfirm, onCancel). Check the parameter definition.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component still doesn't have a props parameter with the required properties. Make sure to add a parameter to the function that includes message, onConfirm, and onCancel.

steps.title: Initialize isOpen state
steps.instruction: Inside the ConfirmationDialog component, use the useState hook to declare an 'isOpen' state variable and initialize it to false.
steps.hint: Call useState(false) and destructure the returned array into a variable and setter function.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have an 'isOpen' state variable that tracks whether the dialog is open, starting as false (closed).
successCriteria: The useState hook is called with false, and the returned array is destructured into 'isOpen' and 'setIsOpen' (or similar setter name).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useState with false and destructuring the array into two variables (e.g., isOpen and setIsOpen).
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. Remember to call useState(false) inside the component and destructure the result.

steps.title: Create openDialog handler
steps.instruction: Inside your ConfirmationDialog component, create a function called openDialog that sets the isOpen state to true.
steps.hint: Define a function that calls setIsOpen with the value true.
steps.expectedOutcome: The openDialog function is defined and ready to be used to show the dialog.
successCriteria: openDialog function is defined and calls setIsOpen(true).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your openDialog function calls setIsOpen with the value true.
steps.feedbackWrong: The openDialog function should set isOpen to true using setIsOpen(true).

steps.title: Add Cancel button with click handler
steps.instruction: Inside the ConfirmationDialog component's return statement, add a Cancel button next to the existing Confirm button. The Cancel button should call the onCancel prop (if provided) and also call closeDialog when clicked.
steps.hint: Add a second button element with an onClick handler that first calls props.onCancel?.( ) and then calls closeDialog().
steps.expectedOutcome: The dialog now has both Confirm and Cancel buttons. Clicking Cancel will trigger the optional onCancel callback and close the dialog.
successCriteria: A Cancel button is added with an onClick handler that calls props.onCancel?.( ) and closeDialog().
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a Cancel button, but make sure it calls both props.onCancel?.( ) and closeDialog() when clicked.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Cancel button is missing or its click handler doesn't properly call both required functions.
